description: How short-form video crushed the internet: Vine fizzled out while YouTube, Instagram Reels and TikTok exploded into the dominant attention platforms. MAUs (millions) compiled from company disclosures, Statista and app-analytics reports — shows one clear winner and one spectacular collapse.
youtube_description:
The Viral Video Takeover — a bar-race through 20 years of attention. This visualization tracks Monthly Active Users (MAUs) for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok (Douyin) and the vanished Vine from 2007–2026. Sources: Google/YouTube disclosures, Meta quarterly user reports, ByteDance public estimates and industry trackers (Sensor Tower, App Annie/SimilarWeb, Statista) and contemporary news on Vine’s 2016 shutdown. The story: Vine peaked fast and died (2016), Instagram scaled from photos to Reels and doubled-down on video, YouTube remained the long-form backbone and continued steady growth, while TikTok exploded from 2017 to become the dominant short-video attention engine. Want the raw race file for your editing? Like + Subscribe, and drop a comment with which beat you want remixed (sound/labels/size). If you recreate this video tag @ourchannel so we can share it!

Sources & notes (high level): company MAU milestones and public reports, Statista aggregate user counts, app-analytics firm estimates. Years where a product didn't exist are 0; Vine post-2016 is 0 after its shutdown. Use responsibly — numbers are compiled from publicly released figures and reputable third-party estimators.
